transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The White House is warning congressional Democrats not to overreach as they follow through on their promise to investigate the Trump administration.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports this is the start of what's expected to be a contentious two years.
In a letter, White House counsel Will Scharf says the administration is monitoring "abusive and capricious threats" made by Democrats.
The letter is addressed to Congressman Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee next year and has suggested Trump aides "lawyer up."
Scharf concludes the administration will not be "extorted" and will not be "cowed" by unlawful process motivated by animus, pettiness or hatred, or any other unlawful motive.
Garcia responded, saying Congress is a "co-equal branch of government" and will not be "deterred" by baseless threats.
Tamara Keith, NPR News, The White House.
The political power shift in Congress could have big implications for air travel. NPR's Joel Rose reports the travel industry is bracing for the possibility of another government shutdown.
U.S. air travelers suffered through three partial government shutdowns over the past two years, with Republicans in charge of the White House and Congress.
Jeff Freeman, the head of the U.S. Travel Association, says it is hard to predict what will happen when Democrats take control of the House and Senate next year.
The unpredictability certainly has us in the mindset of buckle up.
In past shutdowns, TSA officers and air traffic controllers sometimes did not get paid.
Many eventually called out sick and took on second jobs to pay their bills, leading to hours-long security lines as well as delayed and canceled flights.
Freeman says a divided government makes another shutdown more likely.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
Eight Palestinians have been killed in Israeli airstrikes across Gaza over the past 24 hours.
According to Palestinian health officials, a father and his 13-year-old son were killed in a strike on a school sheltering displaced families in Gaza City.
NPR's Anas Baba reports.
The did also include Mahmoud Abdulmanek, a 20-year-old goalkeeper for Gaza's sports club. Another man in his 40s was killed while filling a water tank on the roof of his home in Gaza City, according to Gaza health officials.
Israel's military told NPR it targeted Hamas operatives without providing details.
Gaza's health ministry says more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed during the year-long ceasefire.
For families across Gaza, the danger continues.
From Israeli airstrikes to deadly flooding and landslides, with majorities still displaced and no clear path to safety.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Authorities say the expansion of artificial intelligence is leading to more A.I.-generated hoax calls to 911.
NPR's Jacqueline Diaz reports on how A.I. is affecting the fake calls known as swatting.
The goal with a swatting call is to draw a big response from police to a home, business or school.
It causes a lot of chaos.
People have been injured and even killed as a result.
A.I. now makes it very easy to change a voice or background noise to make a call sound even more realistic and harder to determine what's real and what isn't.
That's a growing concern for 911 dispatchers.
APCO International, the Association of Public Safety Communication Officials, and the Public Safety Threat Alliance published results from a survey done in June.
They received more than 760 responses from 911 dispatchers.
About 14 percent said they were targeted using A.I. tools.
And APCO believes this will increase as A.I. tools continue to advance.
Jacqueline Diaz, NPR News.
Actor Stacey Keach, best known for playing television detective Mike Hammer, has died at the age of 85.
His wife says he died at home in Poland following a long battle with heart disease.
Keach earned a claim on stage, mainly for his performances in Shakespeare's plays.
His screen credits included Nebraska, Blue Bloods, and the sitcom Titus.
He also appeared as the father of George Clooney's character in last year's film, J. Kelly.
This is NPR News.

Travel industry braces for possible government shutdown as Democrats take control of House and Senate
Israeli airstrikes across Gaza kill eight Palestinians in 24 hours, including a father and son at a school
Authorities report AI-generated hoax 911 swatting calls rising, with voice cloning making them harder to detect
Actor Stacey Keach, known for playing detective Mike Hammer, dies at age 85
